name: Supplier Diversification Strategy
consequences: Expanding the supplier base reduces reliance on Apple and Google, enhancing digital sovereignty. However, onboarding new suppliers may introduce integration complexities and require additional regulatory scrutiny.
options: Engage with alternative technology providers to develop a competitive ecosystem for digital identity solutions.
Establish partnerships with local tech startups to foster innovation and reduce dependency on foreign platforms.
Create an open-source initiative that invites contributions from diverse stakeholders to build a community-driven identity solution.
review: Diversifying suppliers can mitigate risks associated with foreign dependency, but it may complicate integration and regulatory compliance efforts.

name: Regulatory Advocacy Framework
consequences: Influencing regulatory bodies can establish platform-neutral requirements, enhancing resilience. However, this may face pushback from established players benefiting from the current system.
options: Draft and propose new regulations that mandate platform-neutral access for digital identity systems.
Collaborate with civil society organizations to advocate for stronger digital sovereignty policies at the EU level.
Engage in public consultations to shape policy discussions around digital identity and supplier concentration risks.
review: Advocating for regulatory changes can strengthen digital sovereignty, but it risks resistance from entrenched interests benefiting from existing frameworks.

name: Technical Demonstrator Development
consequences: Creating non-production demonstrators showcases alternative authentication methods, building credibility. However, limited scope may hinder immediate applicability in real-world scenarios.
options: Develop a mobile demonstrator using open standards to validate alternative authentication methods without relying on major platforms.
Create a browser-based fallback authentication system that operates independently of mobile OS constraints.
Explore hardware token solutions that provide a secure, platform-agnostic authentication method for public services.
review: Demonstrators can provide proof of concept for alternative methods, but their non-production status may limit immediate implementation opportunities.

name: Coalition Building and Stakeholder Engagement
consequences: Building a coalition can amplify advocacy efforts and create a unified front for change. However, aligning diverse interests may slow decision-making processes.
options: Organize workshops with stakeholders to align on shared goals and strategies for digital identity reform.
Establish a formal coalition of civil society, academia, and industry to advocate for platform-neutral solutions.
Conduct outreach to sympathetic members of the Folketinget to gain political support for proposed changes.
review: Coalition building can enhance advocacy impact, but diverse stakeholder interests may complicate consensus and slow progress.

name: Procurement Language Influence
consequences: Shaping procurement language can ensure platform-neutral requirements are included in future contracts. However, existing contracts may resist changes that threaten incumbent interests.
options: Draft model procurement documents that explicitly require platform-neutral access and fallback mechanisms.
Engage with public-sector procurement officials to advocate for changes in tender requirements for digital identity solutions.
Collaborate with EU bodies to align Danish procurement standards with broader European digital identity frameworks.
review: Influencing procurement language can embed platform neutrality in contracts, but existing frameworks may resist such changes.

name: Public Awareness and Education Campaign
consequences: Raising public awareness can build support for digital identity reforms, enhancing political pressure. However, misinformation or apathy may undermine these efforts.
options: Launch a public campaign to educate citizens on the importance of digital sovereignty and platform neutrality.
Host public forums to discuss the implications of current digital identity dependencies and gather community feedback.
Develop educational materials for stakeholders to promote understanding of the risks associated with supplier concentration.
review: Public awareness campaigns can mobilize support for reforms, but overcoming misinformation and apathy may prove challenging.

name: International Collaboration for Standards
consequences: Collaborating internationally can align Denmark's efforts with global standards, enhancing credibility. However, differing national priorities may complicate consensus-building.
options: Engage with international organizations to advocate for global standards on digital identity and platform neutrality.
Participate in EU working groups to influence the development of interoperable digital identity frameworks.
Collaborate with other nations facing similar challenges to share best practices and develop joint advocacy strategies.
review: International collaboration can enhance alignment with global standards, but differing national interests may hinder unified action.

Develop a comprehensive policy proposal that outlines the risks of current dependencies and the benefits of platform-neutral solutions.
Create a public awareness campaign highlighting the importance of digital sovereignty and the risks of vendor lock-in.
review: Advocating for platform neutrality may alienate existing partners who benefit from current vendor relationships, complicating coalition-building and stakeholder engagement.

Collaborate with tech innovators to develop open-source fallback authentication tools that can be widely adopted.
review: Investing in fallback pathways may divert resources from immediate needs, and user adoption could be hindered by familiarity with existing systems.
